sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: Today, from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 今天，从美国的

sentences.en: perspective, North Korea is an existential threat, a hostile nation, dangerously deluded and ready for war.
sentences.zh: 视角来看，朝鲜是一个生存威胁，一个敌对国家，危险地沉浸在妄想中，并随时准备开战。

sentences.en: What's the North Korean perspective?
sentences.zh: 那么朝鲜的视角是什么呢？

sentences.en: A rare interview with the other side.
sentences.zh: 一次与对方的罕见采访。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, October 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月12日，星期四。

sentences.en: Nicholas Kristof, just to start, how do you even get into North Korea?
sentences.zh: 尼古拉斯·克里斯托夫，首先，你是怎么进入朝鲜的？

sentences.en: How did that work?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: So, I've been twice before, and each time afterward, I was banned for a while.
sentences.zh: 我之前去过两次，每次回来后，我都会被禁一段时间。

sentences.en: I had last been in 2005, and so I had tried periodically to get visas again, especially in the last five years and wasn't getting anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我最后一次去是在2005年，所以后来我定期尝试再次申请签证，特别是在过去五年里，但一直没有进展。

sentences.en: And then a year ago, there was a new ambassador to the United Nations.
sentences.zh: 然后一年前，联合国迎来了一位新大使。

sentences.en: I pushed quite hard, invested some effort in negotiating with North Korean diplomats and also, of course, negotiating with another crucial party, my wife.
sentences.zh: 我非常努力地推动，投入了一些精力与朝鲜外交官进行谈判，当然，还要与另一个关键人物谈判，那就是我的妻子。

sentences.en: Who may have feared that this was not the wisest idea.
sentences.zh: 她可能担心这并不是最明智的主意。

sentences.en: You know, look, if your wife is encouraging you to go to North Korea, then that's not a good sign either.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你的妻子鼓励你去朝鲜，那也不是什么好兆头。

sentences.en: So, it finally came through.
sentences.zh: 所以，最终签证办下来了。

sentences.en: We initially were going to go in early September, and then they told us those dates would not work and gave us new dates at the very end of September.
sentences.zh: 我们最初打算在9月初出发，但他们告诉我们那个日期不行，并给了我们9月底的新日期。

sentences.en: Make sure I heard this right.
sentences.zh: 让我确认一下我没听错。

sentences.en: Did you say it took five years, essentially, of negotiations to get into North Korea?
sentences.zh: 你是说为了进入朝鲜，本质上进行了五年的谈判？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's about right.
sentences.zh: 是的，差不多是这样。

sentences.en: That's extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: I have a long history with North Korean officials, and so they know my work, and they're very respectful, but I think they believe that I overemphasize human rights,
sentences.zh: 我和朝鲜官员有很长的交情，所以他们了解我的工作，也非常尊重我，但我认为他们觉得我过分强调人权，

sentences.en: and I think they think I don't fabricate things and am accurate, which they like, but I think they also believe I vastly exaggerate the importance of human rights issues.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他们觉得我没有捏造事实，报道准确，这是他们喜欢的，但我认为他们也觉得我大大夸大了人权问题的重要性。

sentences.en: So, you have a strong sense that North Korea knows exactly who you are, and they're vetting your work, and they're making a determination
sentences.zh: 所以，你有种强烈的预感，朝鲜非常清楚你是谁，他们在审查你的工作，并正在做出决定

sentences.en: about whether you, Nick Kristof, should never be allowed to come back.
sentences.zh: 关于你，尼克·克里斯托夫，是否应该永远被禁止再次入境。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: I've known many of the officials in the America's Department of the Foreign Ministry for years, and the Foreign Ministry seems to be in a bit of an outreach effort these days.
sentences.zh: 多年来我认识外交部美洲司的许多官员，而且外交部最近似乎在进行一些外联工作。

sentences.en: They've invited some other journalists, some scholars, and I think that they are concerned that we may be on a path toward war
sentences.zh: 他们邀请了一些其他记者、学者，我认为他们担心我们可能正走向战争，

sentences.en: and are seeing if they can build some unofficial channels back and forth with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以正在观察是否能与美国建立一些非官方的沟通渠道。

sentences.en: So, I think that was part of how I came to go to Pyongyang.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想这就是我能去平壤的部分原因。

sentences.en: So, you may be part of the diplomacy on the North Korean end is what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，你可能是朝鲜方面外交努力的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, in China, in 1971, you had ping-pong diplomacy that helped deal with the fact that you weren't having official government-to-government contacts to the same degree.
sentences.zh: 在1971年的中国，有过“乒乓外交”，这有助于解决当时你们之间没有同等程度的官方政府间接触的问题。

sentences.en: Literally, athletes, ping-pong players.
sentences.zh: 字面意义上的运动员，乒乓球运动员。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Going through Beijing to break the ice.
sentences.zh: 通过北京来打破僵局。

sentences.en: And these days, there aren't substantial contacts between the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而如今，美国政府和朝鲜政府之间并没有实质性的接触。

sentences.en: government and the North Korean government.
sentences.zh: 我认为朝鲜官员认为，嗯，也许记者可以发挥一些作用。

sentences.en: And I think the North Korean officials think that, well, maybe journalists can help play some role.
sentences.zh: 关于到达那里的后勤工作，你拿到了签证，然后你走的路线是什么？

sentences.en: And just the logistics of getting there, you have your visa, then what's the route that you take?
sentences.zh: 航班是怎么安排的？

sentences.en: What's the flight?
sentences.zh: 你实际上直到最后一刻才能拿到签证。

sentences.en: You don't actually get a visa until the last minute.
sentences.zh: 所以，你的签证获批后，你必须飞往北京。

sentences.en: So, you're approved for a visa and then you have to fly to Beijing.
sentences.zh: 如今，美国禁止美国人前往朝鲜。

sentences.en: These days, there's a United States ban on Americans going to North Korea.
sentences.zh: 所以这也让事情变得复杂。

sentences.en: And so, that complicates it as well.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们需要国务院的批准。

sentences.en: So, we needed State Department approval.
sentences.zh: 我们需要法律的豁免权，这可以因新闻目的而给予。

sentences.en: We needed an exception from the law, which can be given for journalistic purposes.
sentences.zh: 国务院很快就批准了。

sentences.en: And the State Department approved that very quickly.
sentences.zh: 但他们需要给我们一本单独的护照，仅供前往朝鲜的一次旅行使用。

sentences.en: But they needed to give us a separate passport that would be good for one trip to North Korea.
sentences.zh: 所以，飞往北京，我们在那里收到了那张纸，也就是朝鲜签证。

sentences.en: So, flew to Beijing where we received our piece of paper that was a North Korean visa.
sentences.zh: 然后每天大约有一班从北京飞往朝鲜首都平壤的旧式俄罗斯客机。

sentences.en: And then there's about one flight a day on an old Russian airliner from Beijing to Pyongyang, the North Korean capital.
sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，你坐在那架俄罗斯制造的飞机上从北京起飞。

sentences.en: So, Nick, you're in this Russian-made plane flying from Beijing.
sentences.zh: 你在空中注意到了什么？

sentences.en: What do you notice from the air?
sentences.zh: 其实你真的没注意到有什么特别大的不同，你知道，就是田野和森林。

sentences.en: So, you really don't notice anything tremendously different, you know, fields and forests.
sentences.zh: 你真正注意到的是，在飞机上，你周围的每个人都戴着一枚徽章，上面印着国家创始人金日成或他儿子金正日的照片。

sentences.en: What you do notice is that in the plane, everybody around you is wearing a button showing a photo of either the founder of the country, Kim Il-sung, or his son, Kim Jong-il.
sentences.zh: 而且电视屏幕上循环播放着宣传片，展示着……

sentences.en: And they're playing a propaganda loop on the television screen that shows a…
sentences.zh: 所以，不是联合航空的广告之类的。

sentences.en: So, instead of the United ad or whatever.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 那是一场军事音乐会，有非常美妙的古典音乐，但背景中不时有导弹发射的画面。

sentences.en: It's a military concert with really wonderful classical music but missiles periodically going off in the background.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 所以，那真是一个非常诡异的欢迎仪式。

sentences.en: So, that was just a really eerie welcome.
sentences.zh: 一旦你落地，在后勤方面，你在安检和进入街道方面经历了什么？

sentences.en: And once you're on the ground, logistically, what do you go through in terms of security and getting out into the streets?
sentences.zh: 在平壤机场，有一系列移民检查，他们显然对看到美国护照感到有点惊讶，他们看着你，你知道，

sentences.en: So, at Pyongyang Airport, there are a series of immigration controls and they are clearly a little surprised to see an American passport and they look at you, you know,
sentences.zh: 非常严厉。

sentences.en: very sternly.
sentences.zh: 然后你通过海关，他们会检查你所有的东西。

sentences.en: And then you go through customs where they go through everything you have.
sentences.zh: 那是什么样的？

sentences.en: And what did that look like?
sentences.zh: 他们让我把拉杆箱里的所有东西和肩包里的所有东西都拿出来。

sentences.en: So, they had me take everything out of my roller board and everything out of my, you know, shoulder bag.
sentences.zh: 他们想看看每样东西是用来做什么的。

sentences.en: They wanted to see what everything was used for.
sentences.zh: 他们特别想看我带的书籍和书面材料。

sentences.en: They wanted to look in particular at books and written materials that I had.
sentences.zh: 当然，我非常小心，没有带关于朝鲜的书籍之类的东西。

sentences.en: And, of course, I was very careful not to bring in books about North Korea, this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 但我当时正在写一篇关于内分泌干扰化学物质的专栏文章。

sentences.en: But I was working on a column about endocrine disrupting chemicals.
sentences.zh: 所以我带了很多关于环境化学的晦涩出版物。

sentences.en: So, I had a lot of obscure publications about environmental chemistry.
sentences.zh: 所以他们非常仔细地检查了这些。

sentences.en: And so, they looked through those very carefully.
sentences.zh: 他们检查了我的手机，想看看我上面有什么iMovie视频和照片。

sentences.en: They looked through my phone and wanted to see what iMovies I had on it and what photos I had on it.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们会进入应用程序和列表查看？

sentences.en: Oh, they're going into apps and lists?
sentences.zh: 是的，我想他们是在寻找我是否在手机里存储了任何所谓的宗教或反革命材料，以便我随后进行传播。

sentences.en: Yes, I think what they were looking for is if I had stored any maybe religious or counter-revolutionary material, so to speak, on my phone that I would then disseminate.
sentences.zh: 海关人员翻看了我的照片，在我的照片里反复看到了这个看起来很可疑的亚洲女性，显然认为这是某种韩国情报人员在控制我之类的。

sentences.en: And the customs person went through my photos and saw this suspicious-looking Asian woman repeatedly in my photos and clearly thought this was some kind of a South Korean intelligence controller for me or something.
sentences.zh: 然后问，你知道，这是谁？

sentences.en: And said, you know, who's this?
sentences.zh: 我说，我妻子。

sentences.en: And I said, my wife.
sentences.zh: 那位海关官员非常泄气。

sentences.en: And she was very deflated, this customs officer.
sentences.zh: 她只是说，哦，她很漂亮。

sentences.en: She just said, oh, she's very pretty.
sentences.zh: 那是一种罕见的人性化时刻。

sentences.en: It was kind of a rare sort of human moment.
sentences.zh: 那么，当你从酒店出发前往平壤时，向我描述一下你所看到的一些景象。

sentences.en: So, when you set off into Pyongyang from your hotel, describe to me a little bit of what you see.
sentences.zh: 平壤是典型的共产主义首都之一，有宽阔的大街，宏伟的纪念性建筑，几乎没有交通。

sentences.en: So, Pyongyang is one of these classic communist capitals with huge, wide streets, these vast, monumental buildings, and almost no traffic.
sentences.zh: 有一些出租车，我在之前的访问中没见过，它们服务于朝鲜客户。

sentences.en: There are some taxis, which I had not seen on previous visits, and they are serving North Korean clientele.
sentences.zh: 它们在四处巡游，所以它们有一定的汽油供应。

sentences.en: They're cruising around, so they have a certain amount of gas.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，城市景象就是有点诡异。

sentences.en: But, you know, the city scene is just kind of eerie.
sentences.zh: 我们经过金日成和金正日的巨大陵墓，所有的车在经过陵墓时都会减速，以示尊重。

sentences.en: We go by the huge mausoleum for Kim Il-sung and Kim Jong-il, and all the cars slow down as they pass the mausoleum as a sign of respect.
sentences.zh: 还有中学生或高中生的定期游行，通常穿着军装，你知道，试图，我想，

sentences.en: And there are periodic parades of middle school students or high school students, often in military uniforms, you know, trying to, I guess,
sentences.zh: 为他们预期的与美国的即将到来的战争建立勇气。

sentences.en: build courage for the coming war with the U.S., which they anticipate.
sentences.zh: 同样，有一群工人在外面欢呼，鼓励人们努力工作，为与美国的战争做准备。

sentences.en: Likewise, there are a bunch of workers who are out kind of cheering people on to work hard and to prepare for war with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有那些广告牌。

sentences.en: And then you have these billboards.
sentences.zh: 我认为最常见的主题是导弹袭击美国

sentences.en: I say the most common theme is missiles striking the U.S.
sentences.zh: 首都，而且旗帜通常是破烂不堪的。

sentences.en: capital, and often the flag is in tatters.
sentences.zh: 有一个广告牌显示一只朝鲜拳头砸向美国

sentences.en: There is one that shows a North Korean fist smashing down on U.S.
sentences.zh: 导弹。

sentences.en: missiles.
sentences.zh: 另一个显示一辆载有导弹的卡车，上面写着美国

sentences.en: There is another showing a truck with missiles, and it says that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 现在在我们的瞄准镜里。

sentences.en: is now in our crosshairs.
sentences.zh: 还有一个朝鲜士兵踩在一个看起来很懦弱的美国士兵的头上，头盔上有美国

sentences.en: There's one of a Korean soldier stomping on the head of this craven-looking American soldier with a U.S.
sentences.zh: 标志。

sentences.en: on his helmet.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来整个城市在视觉上都是为了反对美国并作为对美国的威胁而存在的。

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds like the whole city exists visually in opposition to and as a threat to the United States.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，看，朝鲜一直很热衷于宣传和宣传场景，但是，你知道，对美国的敌意程度以及这成为一个主题的程度与以前不同了。

sentences.en: And, I mean, look, North Korea has always been big on propaganda and propaganda scenes, but, you know, the level of hostility to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 空气中弥漫着更多的威胁感。

sentences.en: and the degree to which this has emerged as a theme is different from the way it was before.
sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，你住在哪里？

sentences.en: There's much more menace in the air.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不能只是预订酒店之类的。

sentences.en: So, Nick, where were you staying?
sentences.zh: 所以，外交部在接待我们。

sentences.en: You know, you don't just book a hotel or something.
sentences.zh: 他们安排了我们的住宿，把我们安置在平壤郊外稻田里的一个有警卫的外交部大院里。

sentences.en: So, the foreign ministry, they were hosting us.
sentences.zh: 这有点奇怪，因为过去我能够住在平壤市中心的酒店里。

sentences.en: They had arranged our accommodation, and they had put us in a guarded foreign ministry compound outside Pyongyang among the rice paddies.
sentences.zh: 起初，我以为这仅仅是为了把我们与我们可能交谈的朝鲜人隔离开来。

sentences.en: And this was kind of weird because in the past, I'd been able to stay in hotels right in Pyongyang.
sentences.zh: 但渐渐地，显而易见的是，不，

sentences.en: And at first, I thought this was simply to isolate us from North Koreans we might talk to.
sentences.zh: 他们本质上是想保护我们免受情报机构、军方或那些可能不支持这种与美国记者接触的人的伤害。

sentences.en: But gradually, it became apparent that, no,
sentences.zh: 我想确保我理解这一点。

sentences.en: they essentially wanted to protect us from intelligence agencies or the military or people who might not be on board with this kind of outreach to American journalists.
sentences.zh: 你到达了朝鲜。

sentences.en: I want to be sure I understand this.
sentences.zh: 你的向导来自外交部，这听起来像是美国的国务院。

sentences.en: You've arrived in North Korea.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Your guides are from the foreign ministry, which sounds like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 感觉他们可能害怕朝鲜政府内部的其他部门，那些部门可能不想让你在那里。

sentences.en: equivalent of the State Department.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常引人注目的情况。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的，但事实确实如此。

sentences.en: It feels like they may have been afraid of another division of the North Korea's government that might not have wanted to there.
sentences.zh: 我在过去的访问中得到过一些暗示，

sentences.en: This is a pretty remarkable situation.
sentences.zh: 但这次分歧似乎更加明显，在本质上支持接触并了解战争可能有多可怕的后果的外交部人员，

sentences.en: Yeah, but that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 与美国之间。

sentences.en: And I've gotten sort of hints of this on past visits,
sentences.zh: 与美国之间，以及安全机构和军方中的强硬派之间，他们认为这些外交部外交官是与西方人混在一起的软弱之辈。

sentences.en: but the divide seemed much starker at this time between foreign ministry people who are essentially pro-engagement and understand the stakes of just how awful a war might be.
sentences.zh: 他们很软弱。

sentences.en: With the United States.
sentences.zh: 这在许多国家都能看到的动态，但在朝鲜对我来说非常明显。

sentences.en: With the United States and hardliners in the security apparatus and the military who think that these foreign ministry diplomats are wimps hanging out too much with Westerners.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们在大门前，后面的那扇门。

sentences.en: They're soft.
sentences.zh: 那么你能告诉我这次旅行中你早期的行程之一吗？

sentences.en: It's a dynamic you see in a number of countries, but it was very evident to me in North Korea.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一个金正恩建立的新军事博物馆，用来向人们灌输官方意识形态。

sentences.en: So now we are in front of the gate, the gate behind here.
sentences.zh: 所以我们去了这个战争博物馆，这是一个巨大、广阔的广场。

sentences.en: So can you tell me about one of your early stops in this trip?
sentences.zh: 他们有所有这些从朝鲜战争中缴获的美国军事装备。

sentences.en: Well, there is a new military museum that Kim Jong-un built to train people in sort of official ideology.
sentences.zh: 你们现在接待的游客比平时多吗？

sentences.en: So we went to this war museum is vast, sprawling, plaza.
sentences.zh: 有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: They have all this captured American military gear from the Korean War.
sentences.zh: 因为局势紧张，和一年前相比有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Are you getting more visitors now than usual?
sentences.zh: 所以每天大约有3000人参观我们的博物馆。

sentences.en: Is there any difference?
sentences.zh: 我的导游是一位年轻女性，非常有魅力。

sentences.en: Because there are tensions, is there any difference from a year ago?
sentences.zh: 她会说一些英语。

sentences.en: So every day about 3,000 people are visiting our museum.
sentences.zh: 她是一名军官。

sentences.en: My tour guide was a young woman, quite charming.
sentences.zh: 当然，我没有，我不想要战争。

sentences.en: She spoke some English.
sentences.zh: 当然，我没有，我不想要战争。

sentences.en: She was a military officer.
sentences.zh: 当然，我没有，我不想要战争。

sentences.en: Of course, I didn't, I don't want the war.
sentences.zh: 当然，我没有，我不想要战争。

sentences.en: But if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但如果美国

sentences.en: imperialists invaded us and destroyed our country, I will also do all my life, all my things to defend my fatherland.
sentences.zh: 帝国主义者入侵我们并摧毁我们的国家，我也会倾尽一生、竭尽所能去保卫我的祖国。

sentences.en: And her job was to lead people around, including foreigners, and to give them the official propaganda.
sentences.zh: 她的工作是带领人们四处参观，包括外国人，并向他们灌输官方宣传。

sentences.en: Yeah, and is that the museum?
sentences.zh: 是啊，那是博物馆吗？

sentences.en: Normal pictures.
sentences.zh: 普通的照片。

sentences.en: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: And in the museum itself, they have a hall labeled the defeat of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在博物馆里，他们有一个展厅，标着“击败美国”。

sentences.en: They have another about American atrocities against Koreans.
sentences.zh: 他们还有另一个关于美国对朝鲜人暴行的展厅。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's true that there genuinely were some American atrocities against Koreans during the war.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，战争期间美国确实对朝鲜人犯下了一些暴行，这是事实。

sentences.en: There were also North Korean atrocities.
sentences.zh: 朝鲜也犯下过暴行。

sentences.en: I mean, there were plenty of atrocities to go around.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，双方都有很多暴行。

sentences.en: But they argued that there was biological warfare against Koreans by the Americans and that it's pretty clear now is a hoax that that was concocted as propaganda.
sentences.zh: 但他们声称美国人对朝鲜人进行了生物战，而现在很清楚那是一个骗局，是作为宣传捏造出来的。

sentences.en: One of the scenes that just I found kind of saddest was a big diorama showing American corpses being eaten by crows with these, you know, cawing of crows in the background.
sentences.zh: 我发现最令人难过的场景之一是一个巨大的立体模型，展示了美国士兵的尸体被乌鸦啄食，背景中还有乌鸦的叫声。

sentences.en: Did you feel you were being courted by them?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你在被他们拉拢吗？

sentences.en: Were they trying to impress you?
sentences.zh: 他们是在试图给你留下深刻印象吗？

sentences.en: Were they trying to make sure you had a good time?
sentences.zh: 他们是在试图确保你玩得开心吗？

sentences.en: I think the North Koreans wanted us to be welcome.
sentences.zh: 我认为朝鲜人是想让我们感到受欢迎。

sentences.en: But their focus was really on security.
sentences.zh: 但他们的重点确实是在安全上。

sentences.en: And they were repeatedly saying, no, you can't do this.
sentences.zh: 他们反复说，不，你不能做这个。

sentences.en: You can't do that.
sentences.zh: 你不能做那个。

sentences.en: We did ask to see examples of economic reform, which is underway.
sentences.zh: 我们确实要求看一些正在进行的经济改革的例子。

sentences.en: It's a specialty of Kim Jong-un.
sentences.zh: 这是金正恩的专长。

sentences.en: So they did take us to a dolphin show, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确实带我们去看了海豚表演，例如。

sentences.en: A pretty good dolphin show.
sentences.zh: 一场相当不错的海豚表演。

sentences.en: Like a SeaWorld style?
sentences.zh: 像海洋世界那种风格吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是。

sentences.en: It was kind of a North Korean version of SeaWorld.
sentences.zh: 这算是朝鲜版的海洋世界。

sentences.en: And it involved people letting their hair down and yelping with excitement.
sentences.zh: 人们在里面放松心情，兴奋地尖叫。

sentences.en: And then it ended with this huge scenes on big screens of missiles shooting up.
sentences.zh: 最后，大屏幕上播放了导弹发射的巨大场景。

sentences.en: Rather than dolphins jumping.
sentences.zh: 而不是海豚跳跃。

sentences.en: Rather than dolphins jumping.
sentences.zh: 而不是海豚跳跃。

sentences.en: So you got to have a lengthy conversation with a senior foreign policy official in North Korea, Mr. Che.
sentences.zh: 所以你有机会与朝鲜的一位高级外交政策官员崔先生进行了长时间的交谈。

sentences.en: Do you want to sit, Mr. Che?
sentences.zh: 你想坐下吗，崔先生？

sentences.en: Is that okay if you sit there?
sentences.zh: 你坐在那里可以吗？

sentences.en: It looks like a stage.
sentences.zh: 看起来像个舞台。

sentences.en: Who is he?
sentences.zh: 他是谁？

sentences.en: So Mr. Che is the deputy director of the America's division in the foreign ministry.
sentences.zh: 崔先生是外交部美国司的副司长。

sentences.en: And I think he's fundamentally one of the more reasonable guys.
sentences.zh: 我认为他从根本上来说是比较理智的人之一。

sentences.en: He's smart.
sentences.zh: 他很聪明。

sentences.en: He's very well-informed about American affairs.
sentences.zh: 他对美国事务非常了解。

sentences.en: But in our conversation, he took a pretty tough line.
sentences.zh: 但在我们的谈话中，他采取了相当强硬的立场。

sentences.en: And what was the line that he took?
sentences.zh: 他采取的立场是什么？

sentences.en: So on American detainees, including Otto Warmbier, he argued that –
sentences.zh: 关于美国被拘留者，包括奥托·瓦姆比尔，他辩称——

sentences.en: That's a student who was –
sentences.zh: 那是那个学生，他——

sentences.en: This is the University of Virginia student who stole a poster, ended up in a coma in North Korea and dying shortly afterward.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个弗吉尼亚大学的学生，他偷了一张海报，结果在朝鲜陷入昏迷，不久后去世了。

sentences.en: And in the past at times when North Korea has done things like this, it has been willing to express regret.
sentences.zh: 过去，当朝鲜做过类似的事情时，它有时愿意表示遗憾。

sentences.en: And this time, there is no such statement of regret.
sentences.zh: 而这一次，没有任何这样的遗憾声明。

sentences.en: There is no hint of regret.
sentences.zh: 没有任何遗憾的迹象。

sentences.en: What really rubbed me the wrong way was that they boasted about how much money they had spent on his treatment
sentences.zh: 真正让我反感的是，他们吹嘘在治疗他身上花了多少钱，

sentences.en: and how well they had cared for him after he was in a coma, how he didn't have any bed sores.
sentences.zh: 以及在他昏迷后他们照顾得有多好，他身上没有任何褥疮。

sentences.en: Here's a healthy young man who visits the DPRK, commits a crime, and ends up in a coma in a vegetative state on your watch.
sentences.zh: 这是一个健康的年轻人，访问朝鲜，犯了罪，结果在你们的看管下陷入了植物人状态的昏迷。

sentences.en: I must say, that irritated me to be – have a kid who's dead and to be boasting that, well, he didn't get bed sores.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，这让我很生气——一个孩子死了，他们却在吹嘘说，哦，他没有长褥疮。

sentences.en: How can Americans think of that and not feel some kind of deep resentment about the country that arrested him and imprisoned him,
sentences.zh: 美国人怎么能想到这一点而不对那个逮捕并监禁他的国家感到某种深深的怨恨呢？

sentences.en: didn't let his family visit him, didn't let the Swedish ambassador have consular access to him?
sentences.zh: 不让他的家人探望他，不让瑞典大使对他进行领事探视？

sentences.en: And the North Koreans pushed back very hard.
sentences.zh: 朝鲜人进行了非常强硬的反击。

sentences.en: They didn't give an inch of ground on that.
sentences.zh: 在这点上他们寸步不让。

sentences.en: And in fact, they accused the U.S.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们指责美国

sentences.en: essentially of either killing him or allowing him to die simply to make them look bad.
sentences.zh: 本质上是说美国要么杀了他，要么任由他死去，仅仅是为了让他们看起来很糟糕。

sentences.en: The man you're talking to is a foreign policy official at a pretty senior level.
sentences.zh: 你交谈的那个人是一位相当高级别的外交政策官员。

sentences.en: So did you expect and did you maybe even hope that this would be one of the kind of great hopes for diplomatic breakthrough and dialogue?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是否期待，甚至可能希望这会成为外交突破和对话的一大希望？

sentences.en: And what was the reality of that conversation?
sentences.zh: 那次谈话的现实情况如何？

sentences.en: If anybody in North Korea was going to be sympathetic to notions of dialogue and conciliation and talks about talks, it would be people like Mr. Choi.
sentences.zh: 如果朝鲜有人会对对话、和解和谈话的观念表示同情，那应该是像崔先生这样的人。

sentences.en: And in fact, he was pretty tough.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他相当强硬。

sentences.en: So just to clarify, so unless the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以澄清一下，除非美国

sentences.en: were to fundamentally change its policy toward North Korea, you don't see any point in further dialogue and discussions?
sentences.zh: 从根本上改变对朝鲜的政策，否则你认为进一步的对话和讨论没有意义？

sentences.en: He was tough in saying that there is no reason for dialogue now because Trump is denouncing us.
sentences.zh: 他强硬地表示，现在没有对话的理由，因为特朗普正在谴责我们。

sentences.en: The basic message was we are on the brink of a nuclear war.
sentences.zh: 基本信息是我们正处于核战争的边缘。

sentences.en: And this war is not only survivable, but we will win it.
sentences.zh: 而且这场战争不仅是可以幸存的，我们还会赢得胜利。

sentences.en: And you push us and your country is going to be ashes.
sentences.zh: 如果你逼我们，你的国家就会化为灰烬。

sentences.en: And you've got to accept the fact that we are a nuclear power just as much as every other country.
sentences.zh: 你必须接受我们和其他国家一样是核大国的事实。

sentences.en: Mr. Choi, you spoke of us being on the brink of another nuclear war in the Korean Peninsula.
sentences.zh: 崔先生，你提到我们正处于朝鲜半岛另一场核战争的边缘。

sentences.en: Do you really think that North Korea can survive if there is such a nuclear war?
sentences.zh: 你真的认为如果发生这样的核战争，朝鲜能幸存吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: So finally, Nick, if part of the trip was to have these diplomatic conversations, like the one with Mr. Choi, that North Korean and U.S.
sentences.zh: 最后，尼克，如果这次旅行的部分目的是进行这些外交对话，比如与崔先生的那次，而朝鲜和美国

sentences.en: diplomats aren't having, do you think you were successful?
sentences.zh: 外交官们并没有进行这些对话，你认为你成功了吗？

sentences.en: This was a different North Korea than the ones I'd been to before.
sentences.zh: 这是一个与我之前去过的不同的朝鲜。

sentences.en: I was not nervous about going to North Korea previously.
sentences.zh: 以前去朝鲜我并不紧张。

sentences.en: At this time, there was a menace in the air.
sentences.zh: 但这次，空气中弥漫着一种威胁。

sentences.en: There were these billboards showing the destruction of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 到处都是展示摧毁美国的广告牌。

sentences.en: There was much more rhetoric about the U.S.
sentences.zh: 关于美国是敌人的言论多了很多。

sentences.en: as the enemy.
sentences.zh: 关于战争迫在眉睫的言论多了很多，不仅是战争，而且是核战争。

sentences.en: There was much more rhetoric about how war is imminent, not just a war but a nuclear war.
sentences.zh: 关于战争迫在眉睫的言论多了很多，不仅是战争，而且是核战争。

sentences.en: And I left feeling that there is a real risk of a war that would be just catastrophic and that we may be headed for miscalculations on both sides that make a war not likely but a significant possibility.
sentences.zh: 我离开时感到，发生一场灾难性战争的风险是真实存在的，我们双方可能都在走向误判，这使得战争不仅是可能的，而且是极有可能的。

sentences.en: But this would be a war that would be incomparably worse than the Iraq war or the Vietnam war because we are escalating in ways that create a cycle of escalation and we are creating risks of accidents that could just spin out of control.
sentences.zh: 但这将是一场比伊拉克战争或越南战争严重得多的战争，因为我们正在以制造升级循环的方式升级，我们正在制造可能失控的事故风险。

sentences.en: And so I left deeply sobered and alarmed and I think we are way too complacent about a risk of a cataclysmic war ahead.
sentences.zh: 所以我离开时感到非常清醒和惊恐，我认为我们对未来发生灾难性战争的风险太自满了。

sentences.en: Nick, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 尼克，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Hey, it was my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 嘿，这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一个关于热爱设计及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜总会用黑胶唱片当DJ的时代，每天晚上你都要带着300件你最珍贵的财产去工作。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个活生生的、展示精美50年历史文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼的《重塑者》吧。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能看到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他事情。

sentences.en: President Trump has threatened to use the federal government's power over TV licenses to target NBC after a report it aired on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统威胁要利用联邦政府对电视牌照的权力，在NBC周三播出的一篇报道后针对它。

sentences.en: This morning, NBC News has learned striking new details about a July 20th meeting at the Pentagon that preceded Secretary of State Rex Tillerson calling the president a moron.
sentences.zh: 今天早上，NBC新闻获悉了关于7月20日五角大楼会议的惊人新细节，该会议发生在国务卿雷克斯·蒂勒森称总统为白痴之前。

sentences.en: The story reported that in the July meeting, President Trump said he wanted to increase the nation's nuclear weapons stockpile to 10 times its current size,
sentences.zh: 报道称，在7月份的会议上，特朗普总统表示他想将国家的核武器储备增加到目前规模的10倍，

sentences.en: stunning some members of his national security team.
sentences.zh: 这让一些国家安全团队成员感到震惊。

sentences.en: It was after this meeting that Tillerson reportedly made his now infamous comment about Trump.
sentences.zh: 据报道，正是这次会议之后，蒂勒森发表了他现在臭名昭著的关于特朗普的评论。

sentences.en: Speaking from the Oval Office hours later, Trump denied the report.
sentences.zh: 几小时后，特朗普在椭圆形办公室发表讲话，否认了这一报道。

sentences.en: It's frankly disgusting the way the press is able to write whatever they want to write.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，媒体想写什么就写什么，这令人作呕。

sentences.en: And people should look into it.
sentences.zh: 人们应该调查一下。

sentences.en: No, I want to have absolutely perfectly maintained, which we are in the process of doing, nuclear force.
sentences.zh: 不，我想要绝对完美维护的核力量，我们正在这样做。

sentences.en: But when they said I want 10 times what we have right now, it's totally unnecessary, believe me, because I know I know what we have right now.
sentences.zh: 但当他们说我想要我们现在拥有的10倍时，这完全没有必要，相信我，因为我知道我们现在拥有什么。

sentences.en: In a tweet, the president went further.
sentences.zh: 在一条推文中，总统更进一步。

sentences.en: With all the fake news coming out of NBC and the networks, he wrote, at what point is it appropriate to challenge their license?
sentences.zh: 他写道，随着NBC和各大电视网传出的所有假新闻，在什么情况下挑战他们的执照是合适的？

sentences.en: Bad for country.
sentences.zh: 对国家不利。

sentences.en: And the Boy Scouts of America says it will accept girls in a historic shift for the century-old group.
sentences.zh: 美国童子军表示，在这个拥有百年历史的组织中，它将接受女孩加入，这是一个历史性的转变。

sentences.en: I've seen nothing that develops leadership skills and discipline like this organization, said the president of the Boy Scouts.
sentences.zh: 童子军主席说，我没有看到任何像这个组织这样能培养领导技能和纪律的东西。

sentences.en: It is time to make these outstanding leadership development programs available to girls.
sentences.zh: 现在是时候让女孩们也能参加这些出色的领导力发展项目了。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》就是这样。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周在《Wirecutter秀》上，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全遮光才能睡觉的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会因为喝醉而睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是一个非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何地方找到《Wirecutter秀》。
